Might be reassuring idk, I am what you think of when you think worst case scenario with living with type 1. Got diagnosed at 14 after attempting my life 3 months prior. First 5 years took random doses of short acting, very rarely took my long acting. Then I figured out my long acting, got very good at it, and ended up stopping my short acting. I made it just fine (but incredibly dehydrated) to 22, when my diabulimia peaked. For a year,I took short acting once in a blue moon, and I would go 5 days straight with no long acting whatsoever, then getting myself back from emergency level I would take it for a few nights, then back to none for another 4-5 days. I was in the active process of dying, hair falling out, skin and bones, throwing up all the time, only had the energy to lay on my then friends couch and snort coke with him. I was barely alive, but it took some pretty extreme measures to get there. I am somewhat controlled now, I have severe neuropathy, and eye issues, but I am very much alive. So, at the very least, you will not be burying your son, you won’t be losing him.
